net-relief.title: Disaster day

config.setting: A storm has taken down phones and cell towers across the county. You're VE3HAM.

turns.situation: The local emergency coordinator asks if amateurs can help. May you transmit to support relief?

options.text: No: only official emergency stations may
options.feedback: Amateurs may help when normal communications are overloaded, damaged or disrupted.

options.text: Only if the emergency net has been activated
options.feedback: The test is whether normal systems are disrupted.

turns.situation: A fire chief asks you to call the fire department's own radio channel for them.

options.text: Explain you can only use the amateur bands

options.feedback: Using frequencies outside the amateur bands is never permitted, even in relief.

options.text: Do it, but at low power
options.feedback: Power doesn't matter; it's never permitted.

turns.situation: You're not part of the relief net, but want to chat on a frequency next to it.

options.text: Go somewhere else and keep clear of the net
Chat quietly next to the net
options.feedback: Avoid needless transmissions on or near the net frequency.

options.text: Wait until the net is less busy, then use its frequency
options.feedback: Stay away from the net frequency altogether.

turns.situation: On 20 m, where you have no privileges, you hear an unanswered MAYDAY.

options.feedback: In distress almost anything goes; in relief work, the amateur rules still apply.

options.text: Stay silent: you have no privileges there
options.feedback: You may respond to an unanswered distress call on any band.
There's no time, and no need: you may respond.

net-relief.success: In distress almost anything goes; in relief work, the amateur rules still apply.
